html:
El Salvador is the smallest and most crowded country of Central America, on the Pacific coast between Guatemala and Honduras. It has been a separate republic since 1841.

The Pipil people held the land, which they called Cuscatlán, when Pedro de Alvarado invaded for Spain in 1524. Under Spain it was a province of the Kingdom of Guatemala. After independence in 1821 it joined the Federal Republic of Central America, and left when the federation fell apart.

Coffee came to rule the country in the late 1800s. A small group of families owned the best land, while most people were poor farm workers. That split shaped the 20th century:

  • In 1932 a peasant uprising was crushed by the army in the massacre of 1932, known as La Matanza, which killed thousands of mostly Native villagers.
  • In 1969 it fought a short war with Honduras, called the Football War because it broke out during World Cup qualifying games.
  • From 1979 to 1992 the civil war between the army, backed by the United States, and left-wing guerrillas killed about 75,000 people. Archbishop Óscar Romero, a voice of liberation theology, was shot while saying Mass in 1980.

Peace accords in 1992 ended the war. Many Salvadorans had fled to the United States. Gangs that began among them in Los Angeles spread home when members were deported. Since 2019 President Nayib Bukele has jailed tens of thousands of suspected gang members and made bitcoin legal tender. Long before, around 431, the Ilopango eruption buried much of the region in ash.
sum: El Salvador is the smallest and most crowded country of Central America, on the Pacific coast between Guatemala and Honduras. It has been a separate republic since 1841.
